 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. ESPN 's Michael Wilbon is taking an indefinite on-air leave, including "Pardon the Interruption" and his NBA reporting duties.
 Wilbon made the announcement on his X account Monday, Nov. 2, citing "struggles with multiple health issues."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "This isn't retirement, but it is a trip to the injured list," Wilbon wrote. "Hopefully not an extended one. Struggles with multiple health issues in recent months lead me to take an indefinite leave of absence from my PTI and NBA duties at ESPN and ABC."
 MORE: White Sox let go of play-by-play broadcaster for second time in three years 
 Wilbon and his former Washington Post colleague, Tony Kornheiser, have co-hosted "PTI" for 25 years dating to the show's debut on Oct. 22, 2001. He was absent from the show last week, but this is the first suggestion that his absence could be a long one.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 'Bill has come due'
 Team Wilbon coach Michael Wilbon directs his team during the 2020 NBA All Star-Celebrity Game at Wintrust Arena. Mandatory Credit: Quinn Harris-USA TODAY Sports (Reuters)
 "Probably, I should have listened to medical professionals and people closest to me, yep Kornheiser included, who saw worrisome signs in recent years that suggested I take time away earlier. But I didn't," Wilbon wrote. "And as one close friend has said as my issues have become bigger, 'the bill has come due.' The struggles are all health related, not to alcohol (I'm not swearing off the now-and-then Kier Royale) and not to gambling (those winds of change I find loathsome).
 "I have loved sparring and hosting PTI with Tony every single day these past 25 years. And I'm incredibly grateful for the support and encouragement of my colleagues as I take this time away to concentrate on me, specifically on my well-being. I have no idea exactly how this part of my journey will wind up. The goal is to come out of it feeling much better than I do now and ready to return to sparring with Tony."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MORE: Michelle Beadle calls out 'soft' Pat McAfee on 'Dan Le Batard Show' 
 In a statement released by ESPN, chairman Jimmy Pitaro threw his full support behind Wilbon's recovery.
 "Michael and his family have ESPN's full support as he takes time away to focus on his health and well-being," Pitaro said. "He's an important member of our ESPN team and widely respected by his peers, sports fans and so many others throughout our industry. We are here for Michael every step of the way and look forward to welcoming him back whenever he is ready."
